questions.text: Which operation compresses the dynamic range of mel magnitudes while retaining their time-frequency organization?

options.A: Multiplying each waveform frame by a Hann window.
options.B: Taking a logarithm after applying a small positive floor.
options.C: Increasing the hop between successive waveform frames.
options.D: Applying an inverse Fourier transform to each spectrum.

questions.explanation: A logarithm compresses the range of spectral values. A positive floor prevents taking the logarithm of zero.

questions.text: A model was trained on 16 kHz audio using 80 log-mel bins. Your input is 48 kHz audio. Which preprocessing plan preserves the trained input representation?

options.A: Extract 80 bins at 48 kHz and keep all other settings.
options.B: Extract 240 bins at 48 kHz to match the rate ratio.
options.C: Relabel the audio as 16 kHz without resampling it.
options.D: Resample to 16 kHz, then use the training feature settings.

questions.explanation: Proper resampling matches the expected sample rate, and matching the feature settings preserves the trained frontend representation.
